V.rationale: Visa's fundamental health and trajectory are strong: revenue accelerated to $11.23B in Q2 FY2026 (+17.1% YoY), net income grew +31.5% YoY to $6.02B, and operating margins are elite at 64.4%. The franchise is dominant (60% US market share, 5B cards, $15.5T payment volume) with structural tailwinds from cash-to-digital conversion and a fast-growing VAS segment (+27% YoY, 30% of revenue). However, the score is tempered by: (1) a sharp OCF decline to $3.01B (-55.6% QoQ) that introduces cash-quality uncertainty; (2) complete absence of valuation multiples (P/E, EV/EBIT, P/B all n/a in the quantitative pack), making it impossible to confirm the stock is cheap vs. its own history — the qual report's P/S ~14x and 'below five-year average multiples' claims are unverifiable from supplied data; (3) rising rates (10Y at 4.57%) creating multiple-compression headwinds for high-quality compounders; and (4) Berkshire Hathaway's complete exit as a sentiment headwind. The $20B buyback authorization and China access optionality (Trump advocacy on May 15) provide modest near-term catalysts, but neither is a dated fundamental re-rating event. The stock sits at $331.12, -11.8% below its 52-week high of $375.51, which could indicate the market hasn't fully priced the earnings acceleration — but without valuation history this is speculative. Net: excellent business, strong trajectory, but valuation blind spot and OCF weakness cap the score at mildly-to-moderately attractive.
